liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **C.C. Rider** (1 review): The C.C. Rider performance is highlighted as smoking, unlike the reviewer's usual indifference [37]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): This version is described as a rollicking psychedelic stomp that makes others obsolete [33]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-10-21.fob.atm11.chasingwilma.102126.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 192 min [1]
- **gd83-10-21.sbd.bertha-ashley.24998.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 178 min; rated 4.43/5 by 29 [3]. Said about its sound: The Bertha remaster has less bass and a brighter high end than another copy; The recording features punchy midrange, lots of bottom end, and almost no hiss [29][30]
- **gd1983-10-21.164902.senn441.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 173 min [8]
- **gd83-10-21.ficca-brennan.markezin.19516.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 166 min; rated 4.15/5 by 20 [14]. Said about its sound: Silberman's audience recording is cited as one of the finest ever heard; The keys feature smoking fills, and the band's playing is described as spot on [36][38]
- **gd1983-10-21.aud.silberman.348.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 178 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [25]. Said about its sound: The master has a slight glitch in Music Never Stopped and missing encore [25]

## Around the show

- The performance occurred on Brent's birthday, featuring high energy and cosmic moments [27]
- Listeners were kicked out twice for bogus tickets before rushing back in [28]
- The crowd was peaceful, mostly using psychedelics for transportational purposes during the show [34]
- Jerry screamed at the moon from the roof during the fire on the mountain jams [35]
- Girls in the audience had a loud conversation or fight during most of the tune [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-10-21.fob.atm11.chasingwilma.102126.flac16**: taped by chasingwilma; transferred by chasingwilma; source: 3 audio technica atm 11 > sony d-5 Recording Location: FOB dead center [1]. Also: The setlist includes a noodle into Truckin' and a Johnny B. Goode encore [1]
- **gd83-10-21.sbd.bertha-ashley.24998.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>>PCM>>Dat>>CDR>>SHN>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA/SHNThere is another Bertha Remaster of 10/21/83. That version was done with the source that had a cassette gen in the… [3]
- **gd1983-10-21.164902.senn441.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441 mics + (1) Neumann U87 mic blend > Nakamichi 550 [8]
- **gd83-10-21.ficca-brennan.markezin.19516.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Tapes by Ficca and Brennan. Source: Ficca FOB Sony TCD5M with 2 Beyer Dynamic 160's -> Sony CDRW-66>EAC>CDWave>SHN. Encoded by Jake Markezin [14]
- **gd1983-10-21.aud.silberman.348.shnf**: taped by Jeff Silberman; source: FOB (2nd row) Sennheiser 441's > Technics PCM master > DAT [25]

## Art and photos

- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 10/21/83 Centrum, Worcester, M…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26759945313/) [40]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26759945313/) [41]

claims.text: The performance occurred on Brent's birthday, featuring high energy and cosmic moments
Listeners were kicked out twice for bogus tickets before rushing back in
The Bertha remaster has less bass and a brighter high end than another copy
The recording features punchy midrange, lots of bottom end, and almost no hiss
This version is described as a rollicking psychedelic stomp that makes others obsolete
The crowd was peaceful, mostly using psychedelics for transportational purposes during the show
Jerry screamed at the moon from the roof during the fire on the mountain jams
Silberman's audience recording is cited as one of the finest ever heard
The C.C. Rider performance is highlighted as smoking, unlike the reviewer's usual indifference
The keys feature smoking fills, and the band's playing is described as spot on
The setlist includes a noodle into Truckin' and a Johnny B. Goode encore
Rob Eaton recorded and transferred the source, with Charlie Miller coordinating the effort
Girls in the audience had a loud conversation or fight during most of the tune
The master has a slight glitch in Music Never Stopped and missing encore
